about: Ruling 78(f): the one table the 3D game draws its models from. src is own (the country's own model), shared (another country's, by the record; 'of' says whose) or generic. A tag not listed here takes _default. insignia (18 November, Brian's ask for every country's own mark): layers lowest first in a square -1..1: ring [r0, r1], tri [r, turn degrees], star [r, inner, points], rect [u0, u1, v0, v1], each with c (hex); it goes wherever a model's marks say the owner's own; insignia_checked False until the historian confirms it. fin {dir h or v, bands}: the flag's stripes on the rudder. marking_months [{from YYYY-MM, insignia, fin}]: a dominion's wartime roundel and fin flash from that month (fin as above, dir v from the leading edge). On land vehicles an insignia is drawn only inside its disc, radius 1: side bars and anything else beyond it are for aircraft. paint2 is the coat's second colour (the models' upper2 blotches); ground says the home ground it follows; winter_wash: a worn white wash over the coat when the battle's ground is snow. src captured (18 November 2026, Brian's rule for small nations' battleships and carriers): nothing shows until the country holds a great power's plans, by capture or by a spy; then it shows that great power's model named in captured_models[plans].models, in its own hull grey, flying its own ensign (and jack on a battleship). with_plans (ruling 235, b542) on a small nation's bomber or fighter: once it builds four-engined bombers or jet fighters, it draws captured_models[heavybombers or jets].models[the great power capitalPlans names], in its own paint and marking. captured_models keys are the rules' capitalPlans keys; column says which column each serves. Colours are hex. Art director, 16 November 2026. with_tech {tech id: model} shows that model once the country has researched it. swaps {swap name: [[from month YYYY-MM or null for the start, the file's choice], ...]} picks a model's swap by date. carrier_fighter, torpedo_bomber, dive_bomber and carrier_paint are for after release 1, as is a model named under after_release_1.

one_look.about: Brian, 26 November 2026: 'have the paint be on it regardless of the year'. The art director's ruling of the same day: one nation, one mark and one coat for the whole war. Read always; used only with tc.Map.OneLook (or -TheaterOneLook), which is off as it comes. With it on: (1) a country whose mark this table dates (marking_months: AUS, NZL, SAF, IND) wears the LAST of its dated marks, and that mark's fin, in every month; no row of marking_months is changed or read differently with it off. (2) coats: a sculpted model named here wears these colours over its own file's, by the file's paint numbers (0 upper, 1 upper2, 2 under, 3 nose, 4 boss, 6 frame, 15 stain), and number_ink for its side number: a machine that comes into service later wears the coat of the one it follows (follows names it; the seven colours are that model's own). (3) marks: a mark named here is drawn as the other. Checked by Tools/one_look/run.sh against the model files.

Mustang.words: the Warhawk's olive drab over grey, with no nose colour; pale side number

Fw190.words: the Bf 109's two greens over pale blue, and its yellow nose: on her that is the thin ring of the cowling's lip

one_look.marks_words: the American star in its blue disc with the red centre (the Warhawk, the Dauntless) is drawn as the star and bar, a white bar each side edged in blue and no red anywhere, as the B-17 and the Mustang wear it. It is the mark of the newer B-17 picture Brian approved on 25 November 2026 (art director, 26 November, 21:42Z; the red-centre ruling of 04:16Z that day is withdrawn). Vehicles keep the army's plain white star. The German cross (GER) is drawn at its real proportions (GER-BALKEN): black bars a quarter of its length wide, white an eighth each side, a thin black edge a thirty-second outside the white, nothing across an arm's end, on aircraft, tanks and the map's pieces alike: one nation, one mark (Brian, 26 November 2026, 21:45Z: 'the german logo is wrong on the FW-190'; art director, 27 November, 01:11Z). No file carries GER-BALKEN: it is the painter's own.
